speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, when did you first notice the yellowish coloring of your skin and eyes, and have you experienced any abdominal pain or changes in the color of your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any fever, nausea, or right upper quadrant pain, and have you noticed dark urine or pale stools? I will also check for hepatomegaly or tenderness in your abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe liver dysfunction with a prothrombin activity under 40% and agitation, you are exhibiting signs of acute liver failure. I need to know if you have experienced any confusion, difficulty staying awake, or muscle twitching in the past 24 hours?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: The agitation and confusion you are experiencing suggest hepatic encephalopathy, a serious complication of acute liver failure. I need to rule out acute hepatitis B infection, which can present with severe liver dysfunction despite initial negative screenings, so I am requesting a specific HBsAg and IgM anti-HBc test. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_Specific_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the specific viral panels and toxicology screens have returned no findings, I need to investigate other causes of acute liver failure. Do you have any history of autoimmune disorders, and have you taken any herbal supplements or unknown substances recently? REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of acute liver failure, agitation, and a history of ecstasy use strongly suggests toxic hepatitis, likely from contaminants in the illicit substances or heat stroke-related injury. DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Liver Failure secondary to toxin-induced hepatitis (likely ecstasy/cocaine related)
